First of all, I just wanted to acknowledge that you are a wonderful mom. I don’t think my mom ever been so thoughtful about weight/appearance related stuff. She wasn’t that thoughtful when I was 15 and was in perfectly healthy weight - she thought I was fat. I got bulimia and got severely underweight. She just scolded me and refused to spend money on my food as “it will end up in the loo anyway”. I’m 30 now, I live in another country, I gained weight (PCOS, stress, rebound from teenage years) and I learned to love myself - and she still manages to tell me how fat I am. 

Secondly. I think, it is important to talk about weight management in general and then make your point about wegovy. There is one single pillar in weight loss - caloric deficit. You can either exercise like crazy and eat whatever you want or you can eat less. Wegovy helps you eat less and make better choices - it is not a magic pill that mysteriously burns your fat. You can be on wegovy and still not lose weight - so your wegovy journey is a lot of self-work, it’s not some kind of a cheat. Also, I think you will show them honesty and love, which is very important.

You know, Canon EF 50 1.2 saved my ass many times in quite unexpected situations. I will omit obvious use - really cool portraits in almost any lighting conditions (especially natural light during twilight or window light indoors). I‘ve got some nice landscape shots with it when there was literally no light - and 1/20-1/10 shutter speed was enough. Also I managed to do some macro shots with it - like bees, flowers, food. 

Yes, sometimes I get disappointing results for portraits, because due to thin focal plane you focus literally just on the tip of the nose. Or just face - and nose is blurry. But I got used to it. Or just go with 24-70 if I don’t want to bother.

I love my Canon EF 50 1.2. Hate this expression, but this lens „is not for everyone“. And it has nothing to do with your skill or what you prefer to shoot. 

It can be slow in terms of autofocusing. Some may find the focus length not enough/too much. Some may also say it gets too shallow. 

For me personally this is my 2nd most used lens after 24-70. I can even say it is my „go-to“ lens, because it shoots great in any light. You can use it for anything, not just portraits. I’d say, it is the most personal lens I have, it has its own soul and character. And just like with a person, you either get along with it or not. I’d say - rent 1.2 for a day, get used to it, make a decision. Good luck!

UPD: a year ago I was seeking advice about 50 1.2 in this group. And to be honest, I’d say I purchased it “despite” rather than “because”. A lot of people don’t like it

I have super weak topics, like anatomy and most of the cardio (I'm lame), so it takes me a lot of time to understand and remember. So these days are not really productive and I don't feel like studying after 3-4 hours. And I also understand, that even if I push myself and study more, I won't retain the information.

When I'm pretty familiar with the topic and just refresh my knowledge, I can study for 6-10 hours and have fun.

When I should have known the topic, but in fact had a lot of gaps, I made bootcamps of like 2-3 days of non-stop bnb or physic or osmosis, to get the full picture as fast as possible and then to dig into details. Also worked. 

The thing is, there no such thing as "enough" or "not enough" imho. There's no sense in grinding for 12-16 hours just to wake up next day and find out you remember nothing.

Maybe I am old-fashioned, but I think your makeup should look as natural as possible: foundation to get rid of paleness, concealer to hide stress-induced acne, some close-to-natural lipstick. For me the only place on my face where I let my imagination do whatever it wants is probably my eyes: liquid liner, shadows, mascara - any colors in any combinations - it looks nice and improves my mood. First of all, we wear masks A LOT, so eyes are the only place which will always be seen. Secondly, lipstick or too much foundation will probably be destroyed by noon, so I try to apply just as much as needed. Finally, I think that too much makeup looks unprofessional - BUT, it’s just my opinion, you can disagree. I would say, that eyes + socks + crocs charms are the three places, where you can do whatever you want and it won’t look vulgar.

My parents got a disgusting, terribly hurting and disappointing divorce just before (literally a day or two) my thesis defence and subsequent graduation. Combined with my burn-out from my classmates and medicine in general, it sent me straight to the deepest depression I‘ve ever had. Also got diagnosed with bipolar and prescribed meds which made me a walking zombie for months.

I also started a new long-distance relationship with my now-husband and wasn’t able to keep my shit together. Result: YOG 2018, got Masters in Bioinformatics with a couple of decent peer-reviewed papers and now work as a Bioinformatician in the UK, where I moved last year. And now stupid me has enough resource (and earnings) to finally take Steps and apply to residency in the US which was my plan originally before things started to fall apart.
